leagues.name: United Rugby Championship
leagues.where: Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Italy and South Africa
leagues.how: Sixteen clubs from Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Italy and South Africa play an 18-round league from September to May. The top eight reach the quarter-finals, then semi-finals and a Grand Final in June. The higher-ranked side is at home in every play-off, the final included.

leagues.name: Premiership Rugby
leagues.how: Ten English clubs play each other home and away: 18 rounds from September to May. The top four reach the semi-finals, first v fourth and second v third at the higher-ranked club, and the final is at Twickenham in June.

leagues.name: Premiership Women's Rugby
leagues.how: England's top women's league. The clubs play each other home and away, then the top four reach the semi-finals and the final.

leagues.name: Top 14
leagues.how: Fourteen French clubs play 26 rounds from September to June. The top two go straight to the semi-finals; third to sixth play off for the other two places, and the final is in late June. The bottom club goes down to Pro D2, and 13th plays off to stay up.

leagues.name: Super Rugby Pacific
leagues.where: New Zealand, Australia, Fiji and Samoa
leagues.how: Clubs from New Zealand, Australia, Fiji and Samoa play a regular season from February to May. The leading teams go through to the finals series, which ends with the final in June.

leagues.name: Currie Cup
leagues.how: South Africa's provincial championship, played in the southern winter: a round-robin league, then the top four play semi-finals and a final.

leagues.name: National Provincial Championship
leagues.how: Fourteen New Zealand provinces play ten matches each from August to October. The top eight reach the quarter-finals, then semi-finals and a final, with the higher-ranked side at home.

leagues.name: Japan Rugby League One
leagues.how: Japan's top division runs from December to May. After the regular season the top six reach the play-offs, which end with the final in late May.

leagues.name: European Rugby Champions Cup
leagues.how: Europe's top club competition: 24 clubs, eight each from the URC, the Premiership and the Top 14, in four pools of six. Each club plays four pool games, against the clubs from the other two leagues. The top four in each pool reach the round of 16, then come the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final. Fifth place drops into the Challenge Cup knockouts.

leagues.name: EPCR Challenge Cup
leagues.how: Europe's second club cup: the clubs that miss the Champions Cup, plus invited teams, in pools of six, four pool games each. The top sides in each pool reach the round of 16, joined by the four clubs that finished fifth in their Champions Cup pools; then come the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final.
